text:
adrian: Heads-up — we're prototyping an in-console warning when someone grants a role with wide routing/quota scopes (eg. `*` routes or cross-tenant quotas). Want feedback on copy + rollout telemetry.

sara: +1. Core question: do we block the grant or just surface a soft warning? For enterprise customers we probably need a second confirmation step.

ben: My vote is soft warning by default, with an enforceable policy toggle for org admins. We shouldn't break automation.

maria: Agree. Also need to track what they clicked — dismiss vs confirm vs open docs. That telemetry will drive whether copy works.

ux-emma: Draft copy idea: "This role can access all routes and billing quotas. Consider scoping to the minimum required routes to limit blast radius." Buttons: "Cancel", "Scope now", "Grant anyway". Inline link to a short how-to.

adrian: Love the microcopy. Two UX asks: (1) if they choose "Scope now" bring up quick-scope modal with route chooser & search, (2) if "Grant anyway" prompt a tiny justification field for audit logs (optional for non-enterprise).

ben: For backend we should add a new API field on grants: `pregrant_warning_shown: boolean`, `pregrant_decision: enum` and `justification: string`. Also return `scoped_routes_preview` for the modal.

maria: Telemetry events I suggest: `scope_warning_shown`, `scope_warning_dismissed`, `scope_warning_confirmed`, `scope_quick_scope_used`, `scope_justification_submitted`. Include role_id, actor_id, tenant_id, and a hashed route fingerprint (not raw route list) for PII.

sara: Small privacy note — don't send full tenant IDs in client-side telemetry for public cloud. Use account-hash or backend-sampled events.

ux-emma: UI detail: show a compact inline badge when a role contains any wildcard scope: "Wide scope" with tooltip. Badge links to the same modal.

adrian: Rollout plan: feature-flag gated + 10% of orgs for 2 weeks, then widen. For enterprise orgs: set flag off by default and enable in console rollout with an opt-in prompt to test. Will add canary logs for false positives.

ben: Can we add a console-only flag for the soft vs hard mode so we can test enforcement in staging? `scope_warning_mode: soft|hard|off` per org.

maria: Yes. Also capture `ui_variant` in events to A/B copy. We'll need a short eval script to check if quick-scope reduces grants with wildcard.

sara: Security question — if someone bypasses the warning and scripts it away (API grant), should the API return a 200 but emit an audit-level alert? I think yes.

adrian: Proposed: API accepts grants, but if `wide_scope_detected && org_policy_enforce == true` return 409 requiring explicit `force=true` and justification. Otherwise 200 and emit high-severity audit event.

maria: Sounds good. I'll draft the telemetry schema and hash rules. Ben, can you sketch the API changes? UX: Emma will mock the modal.

ben: I'll post a quick PATCH example in #eng-platform-apis after lunch. Sample:
```
PATCH /v1/orgs/{org}/roles/{role}/grants
{
  "routes": ["*"],
  "pregrant_warning_shown": true,
  "pregrant_decision": "grant_anyway",
  "justification": "needed for onboarding scripts"
}
```

ux-emma: Nice. One more tiny ask: show estimated cost impact in modal when quota is wide (approx tokens/hr) — even a rough number nudges people to scope.

adrian: Great idea. We'll wire estimated-usage into the preview call. Ok next steps: Emma mock + Maria telemetry schema + Ben API proto + Feature flag config. Ping me when ready and I'll schedule a short rollout sync.

deploy-bot: Note: Feature flag created `ff.scope_warning_v1` (off by default) — admin can opt-in for enterprise orgs.

sara: Thanks all. Quick follow-up: who owns docs? I can write the short how-to once Emma's mock is done.

ux-emma: I'll drop the mock in Figma and link it here when ready.

adrian: Thanks team — this feels actionable. We'll try to keep modal minimal and non-blocking unless org policy requires enforcement. :thumbsup:
